charges: Providing material support to terrorist organizations
sentence: Detained in the UK from 2004 pending a US extradition approved in 2005 and carried out in 2012; held roughly two years in a US Supermax in solitary confinement, then sentenced largely to time already served and released a few months later.

charges: Charges related to relaying police-scanner information to protesters via Twitter at the 2009 G-20
sentence: Arrested at the 2009 G-20 in Pittsburgh for using a police scanner and Twitter to help protesters avoid police; his Queens home was raided by the FBI/Joint Terrorism Task Force on Oct. 1, 2009. Released shortly after.

charges: Conspiracy / murder in connection with the 1971 killing of an SFPD sergeant (San Francisco 8)
sentence: As 'Cisco' Torres, a NYC-based former Black Panther and Vietnam veteran, he was among the San Francisco 8 charged in 2007 over the 1971 killing of SFPD Sgt. John Young; the case collapsed and charges against him were dismissed.

Scapegoated after the 1993 Lucasville (Southern Ohio Correctional Facility) uprising despite being in a different wing; refused a plea and was the first defendant tried on murder charges. Still incarcerated, with next parole eligibility reported as 2061.

charges: Conspiracy / murder in connection with the 1971 killing of an SFPD sergeant (San Francisco 8)
sentence: Former Black Panther arrested in 2007 at his Altadena home as part of the San Francisco 8 case over the 1971 killing of an SFPD sergeant; an earlier 1970s prosecution had been thrown out over torture-obtained evidence, and after extensive pretrial litigation the charges against him were dismissed in 2009.

charges: Conspiracy / murder in connection with the 1971 killing of an SFPD sergeant (San Francisco 8)
sentence: Living in Panama City, Florida, he was one of the former Black Panthers arrested in January 2007 when the 1971 case was revived; after extended litigation and a narrowing of the prosecution, the charges against him were dismissed in 2009.

Convicted of illegally sending large sums abroad through an unlicensed company (alleged, but unproven, to fund terrorism) and given the maximum 5-year prison term. A leader in Lackawanna's Yemeni-American community; later elected to city council (2017) but barred from office over the crime of 'moral turpitude.'

charges: Immigration/marriage fraud; unauthorized access of an FBI computer
sentence: Former CIA/FBI employee who admitted in court to counts tied to a sham marriage used to obtain U.S. citizenship and to unauthorized use of an FBI computer; she later said she felt pressured into the plea by threats including deportation to Lebanon.

charges: Trespass / civil disobedience at nuclear weapons facilities and military installations
sentence: Mennonite peace activist in the Catholic Worker / Plowshares tradition, repeatedly arrested for civil disobedience at U.S. nuclear weapons facilities and military installations; his arrests appear in the Nuclear Resister's Inside & Out roster.

charges: Trespass at Vandenberg Air Force Base
sentence: Convicted of trespass for a May 2001 backcountry occupation of Vandenberg AFB protesting U.S. 'Star Wars' (National Missile Defense) missile-defense tests; served approximately 3 months.

Arrested May 22, 2002 at an anti-Iraq-war demonstration in Santa Cruz targeting Rep. Sam Farr; charged with felony battery and resisting arrest after police sparked a melee. Sentenced to nine months in the Santa Cruz County Jail, plus 30 days added for refusing transfer to minimum security; began serving Nov. 23, 2002 in Unit K.

charges: Conspiracy to provide material support to al Qaeda
sentence: Bronx martial-arts instructor arrested in a post-9/11 undercover terrorism sting; pleaded guilty to conspiring to provide material support to al Qaeda, admitting he agreed to train fighters in hand-to-hand combat and pledged allegiance to Osama bin Laden. Sentenced in federal court (Manhattan) to 15 years.

charges: Attempted murder, assaulting a police officer, forcible confinement
sentence: Mohawk activist of Six Nations of the Grand River named in the 2006 Caledonia land reclamation (occupation of Douglas Creek Estates); warrants were issued for him over confrontations tied to the dispute, with reported charges including attempted murder, assaulting a police officer, and forcible confinement.
